subject: ANOVA with nested random and fixed effects: help!

messages.author: 7e208d26917e9ea2
messages.subject: ANOVA with nested random and fixed effects: help!
parts:
Hello R friends,

I am stuck on an analysis I'm doing for my advisor's experiment that involves an anova with multiple layers of nesting of random and fixed effects. In this experiment, there are three sites, with five blocks per site. Each block is divided into two watering treatments (plots), and in each plot there are two priority planting treatments (sub-plots). So, it's kind of a split-split plot design, but I was advised to analyze this as a repeated measures experiment, with blocks counting as the repeated measures. Block is the only random factor, and site, water, and planting treatment are fixed effects.

We want to test the effects of planting treatment, watering treatment, site, and all 2- and 3-way interactions on native and invasive plant cover using anova. The thing that seems to be tripping me up the most is the fact that there's a random effect (Block) sandwiched between fixed effects, (the nesting structure goes: Site/Block/Water/Planting Treatment), and I don't know how to code this properly.

I suspect that we may not have enough degrees of freedom to analyze this correctly. Another option is to ignore the nesting of block within site, which would make blocks simple replicates of the water*planting treatment combinations.(Technically this is pseudoreplication, but it could also be thought of as a stratified random sample of sites.)

I have been trying to use lme from the nlme package. (Apparently lme4 does not give p-values, and we want those.) My consultations with a statistician and myriad online and print resources have resulted in a number of attempts, but I am not convinced any of them are correct. Maybe you can help!

Here are some attempts so far:

#This one ignores nesting of block within site, but includes the other levels of nesting
mod1=lme(Cover~ Site*Water*PlantingTrt,
          random=~1|Block/Water/PlantingTrt)

#This one includes the full nesting structure, but I'm not sure everything should go in the random statement. Plus I get NaNs for Site.
mod2=lme(Cover~ Site*Water*PlantingTrt,
          random=~1|Site/Block/Water/PlantingTrt)

#This one uses the aov function instead, and I got this code from this example. The results are very different from anything above.
mod3 = aov(Cover ~ Site * Water * PlantingTrt + Error(Block/Site:Water))


I would greatly appreciate any advice on this!

Thanks,
Emily

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Re: ANOVA with nested random and fixed effects: help!
parts:
OK, I have a quick, perhaps point missing question: 
Are the watering and planting treatments really different per block? 

It seems surprising if they are, but if they're not, and if you were specifying RE on them, I think you would be in the territory of crossed effects (i.e. the the watering or planting treatments not being properly nested within site, or at least within block). BUT, it sounds to me like you don't want any RE on either water or planting. 

Now, my take: 

From your description you don't want RE on Site either, so in that case my interpretation of the question is how to specify RE on block alone, which is: 

mod4  = lme(Cover ~ Site*Water*PlantingTrt, random=~1|Block)

This corresponds to a model where observation i in block j of site k

Cover_i,j,k ~ Intercept + Site_k*Water_i*Planting_i + Intercept_j

where Intercept_j ~ Normal(0, sigma_block) # where sigma_block estimated across all blocks. 
I believe the lme code above for mod4 would do this so long as every block has a unique number. 

Also see the recent paper in methods in ecology and evolution relevant to this issue:
- Schielzeth, Nakagawa_2013_Nested by design model fitting and interpretation in a mixed model era

- Jaime

parts:
Thanks for the comments thus far!

Jaime- To answer what I think is your question, there aren't major differences in treatment effects across different blocks, but there are some, particularly for one site. One thing mod4 doesn't do is specify the fact that planting treatment is nested in the watering treatment. Because block is first split into watering treatment, and then planting treatments are randomized within watering treatment, this becomes a split-plot design. I think I need to specify random~1|Block/Water/PlantingTrt to do this, otherwise we run into pseudoreplication issues (which may or may not be that egregious depending on your perspective).

To illustrate, and answer Miguel's question, here are some results:

mod4
anova(lme(Cover~ Site*Water*PlantingTrt, random=~1|Block)

PlantingTrt                    1    36   63.13457  <.0001
Site:Water                    2    36    3.45846   0.0423

Site:Water:PlantingTrt    2    36    3.62124  0.0369


mod1
anova(lme(Cover~Site*Water*PlantingTrt, random=~1|Block)

                      numDF denDF  F-value p-value
(Intercept)                  1    24  94.98057  <.0001
Site                           2    12  12.97288  0.0010
Water                        1    12   4.48035  0.0559
PlantingTrt                  1    24  70.22745  <.0001
Site:Water                  2    12   3.14120  0.0800
Site:PlantingTrt            2    24  15.00748  0.0001
Water:PlantingTrt         1    24   9.26547  0.0056
Site:Water:PlantingTrt  2    24   4.02807  0.0310

I'm pretty confident now that mod 1 is correct, given the experimental design. But NOW what's throwing me for a loop is the fact that when I try to run this using Type III sums of squares instead of the default Type I, I get really different results! This is a balanced design, so I assumed it should be the same, but I guess there's something about the nestedness that makes it weird. For example:

anova on mod1 using Type III SS
anova.lme(mod1, type = "marginal")
                        numDF denDF  F-value p-value
(Intercept)                  1    24  0.00169  0.9675
Site                            2    12  0.25786  0.7769
Water                         1    12  0.02116  0.8868
PlantingTrt                   1    24 78.63242  <.0001
Site:Water                   2    12  0.14417  0.8672
Site:PlantingTrt             2    24 17.29196  <.0001
Water:PlantingTrt          1    24 14.25196  0.0009
Site:Water:PlantingTrt    2    24  4.02807  0.0310

"Site" goes from p=0.001 to 0.78! And everything changes but the 3-way interaction. What's up with that?? This may be more of a stats question than an R question, but I'd happily take any advice on why I'm getting such different results with Type I and III SS. (By the way, by looking at the data, it seems that "site" should in fact be significant, so I am trusting the Type I results more.)

Thanks again,
Emily

parts:
After reading several posts in Cross Validated, I am still very confused about the nesting structure. But it appears that ~1 | block basically means Block is the only random effect and has the same variance across all other levels.
But one other thing I notice is if site and plantingTrt are categorical data, then the output of you result should have some dummy variables but not what is shown in your result, so maybe you should change the numeric to factor?
Last, I think using 'marginal' might be more appropriate, it seems like sequential is used if you assume the effect is additive (i.e no interaction) which is not the assumption in your case. But I am not 100% sure.
Currently I am taking the class that teaches us mixed model, so I should consult with professor to more adivise.

messages.author: 7e208d26917e9ea2
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Re: ANOVA with nested random and fixed effects: help!
parts:
Yu Pei (and others),

I got some more advice on how to do this, and what was recommended to me was assigning a new variable with a unique main plot ID (as a reminder, watering treatments are assigned to main plots within blocks, and planting treatments to subplots within main plots), and then specifying the random statement like this:

random=~1|Block/MainPlot

Turns out, this gives me the same results as specifying the error term like this (as I had done before):

random=~1|Block/Water/PlantingTrt

This might be because I only have one replication of water*planting treatment per block, but it is a good sign! (I suspect the first way might be the best way to do it if I had replications within blocks, but I haven't actually thought this through. I should also note that I assigned unique IDs to blocks, and told R they were factors. All the effects are factors.)

I was also told that Type I (sequential) SS were best for this design, so that is also good.

I think I'm all set on this now, but it's been fun geeking out with you all!

Thanks,
Emily
